package.name: statgrab
package.summary: PHP bindings for libstatgrab: CPU, memory, disk, network, and process metrics.
package.description:
PHP bindings for libstatgrab (https://libstatgrab.org), the cross-platform system-statistics library. Reads CPU usage, memory and swap, disk I/O, filesystem space and inode counts, network interface counters, page-in/out, process tables, logged-in users, and host metadata. Works on glibc Linux, musl, macOS, FreeBSD, NetBSD, OpenBSD, and Solaris.
Two API surfaces ship in parallel: a procedural one matching the original 2006 PECL release (sg_cpu_percent_usage, sg_memory_stats, sg_process_stats, ...) and a Statgrab class with method-based access and class constants for sort orders, process states, and duplex modes. Both surfaces emit E_WARNING and return false on libstatgrab errors; the OO surface throws on argument-count violations. sg_error_details() returns array{code,errno,message,arg} from libstatgrab (or false when no error is pending); the OO surface exposes the same shape via Statgrab::errorDetails().
The repo also ships a vendored libstatgrab 0.92.1 with local patches for an sg_destroy_globals off-by-one that leaks the user-stats vector at process exit, a stack buffer overflow in the diff getters when the device count shrinks, and uninitialised process session IDs (none in an upstream release yet), plus a local fix for two undefined shifts. Configure with --with-statgrab=bundled to statically link the patched copy without waiting on system packages.
Requires libstatgrab >= 0.92 and PHP >= 8.0 (NTS or ZTS).
package.notes:
Thread-safety and bundled-library hardening.
- Under ZTS, sg_fs_stats(), sg_valid_filesystems(), and sg_set_valid_filesystems() are serialized across threads; concurrent calls could use freed memory in libstatgrab's process-wide list. - Bundled libstatgrab carries upstream fixes for a stack overflow in the network and disk diff getters (libstatgrab#148) and uninitialised session_id values on Linux (libstatgrab#147), plus two undefined-shift fixes. - proc_title in sg_process_stats() rows is capped at 4096 bytes. - A bundled build no longer silently links the system libstatgrab after make clean. - A memory_limit error while building process or filesystem arrays no longer leaks libstatgrab's result buffer.
See CHANGELOG.md for the full list.
